en.1896_McKinley_Reed/questions_json/166@0/: What points do you wish to touch upon as you accept the Republican nomination? A written transcript will be transmitted to voters across the country.
en.1896_McKinley_Reed/questions_json/165@1/: Which of the following will be your primary campaign message?
en.1896_McKinley_Reed/questions_json/184@2/: Will you send campaigners to Nebraska, in an attempt to deliver an embarrassing defeat to Bryan, or should those resources be focused on South Dakota, Wyoming, and Iowa?
en.1896_McKinley_Reed/questions_json/167@3/: Bryan's nomination has electrified the western voter, and he is now planning to campaign on the rails, six days a week. Will you break precedent as well and make a speaking tour of the nation?
en.1896_McKinley_Reed/questions_json/195@4/: The United States is in the midst of a financial calamity, with masses of unemployed men on the streets. What will you do to revive business in this country?
en.1896_McKinley_Reed/questions_json/170@5/: You have the support of the important newspapers, and they are willing to accept your guidance on the proper campaign message. What do you want them to print?
en.1896_McKinley_Reed/questions_json/182@6/: Some of the border states (Virginia, Maryland, Kentucky) are very close this year. Do you have a strategy to make these states jump to the Republican side?
en.1896_McKinley_Reed/questions_json/194@7/: What is your definitive position on the tariff issue?
en.1896_McKinley_Reed/questions_json/196@8/: Grover Cleveland sent federal troops to Illinois to end the Pullman Strike without the request of Governor Altgeld. Was this an overreach on his part?
en.1896_McKinley_Reed/questions_json/193@9/: Can you state your definitive position on the American monetary system?
en.1896_McKinley_Reed/questions_json/197@10: What is your opinion on measures that would aim to restrict the sale or production of alcohol?
en.1896_McKinley_Reed/questions_json/179@11: The West Coast is a very competitive region. Can you make the case for Republican policies there, particularly in those places such as San Francisco which rely on foreign trade?
en.1896_McKinley_Reed/questions_json/206@12: What is your interpretation of the antitrust statutes? Do large American business profit from monopolistic practices?
en.1896_McKinley_Reed/questions_json/241@13: Do you think that local jurisdictions should be allowed to use hanging or other forms of capital punishment for crimes?
en.1896_McKinley_Reed/questions_json/171@14: John Palmer, a Gold Democrat, is also running against Bryan. He has offered to remove his name from the ballot on the East and West Coast if you will do the same in the South. He argues that this will consolidate the anti-Bryan vote. What do you think?
en.1896_McKinley_Reed/questions_json/250@15: Is it generally appropriate for federal courts to issue injunctions against striking unions?
en.1896_McKinley_Reed/questions_json/237@16: Do you think that there should be federal oversight of the New York and Chicago trading markets?
en.1896_McKinley_Reed/questions_json/198@17: Grover Cleveland led the push to repeal the Sherman Silver Purchase Act in 1894. What are your thoughts on his actions during that period?
en.1896_McKinley_Reed/questions_json/220@18: Some labor leaders have called for regulation standardizing a ten or even an eight hour workday. Do you support these calls?
en.1896_McKinley_Reed/questions_json/202@19: The Wilson-Gorman Tariff Act of 1894 lowered the rates on many goods, while still falling well short of Cleveland's ideal levels. What do you think about this act as a whole?
en.1896_McKinley_Reed/questions_json/232@20: In general, is the Supreme Court too obstructionist in their rulings on economic issues? Would you appoint judges who would bring a new perspective to these issues?
en.1896_McKinley_Reed/questions_json/219@21: Would you support a program to compensate workers who are injured on the job? Is this a proper responsibility of the federal government?
en.1896_McKinley_Reed/questions_json/169@22: What do you have to say about William Jennings Bryan's campaign, at a high level?
en.1896_McKinley_Reed/questions_json/207@23: Should there be greater regulation or even price controls on railroad shipping rates?
en.1896_McKinley_Reed/questions_json/192@24: There is one week left until election day. Every state is important, but where will you give an extra push with what is left of your financial resources to educate the American voters?
en.1896_McKinley_Reed/answers_json/1479@0/d: I am a proud "wet" in the alcohol debate. What a man drinks is no one's business but his own.
en.1896_McKinley_Reed/answers_json/1352@1/d: My opponent's ideas are almost as dangerous to the survival of the United States as the Democratic traitors were in the 1860s.
en.1896_McKinley_Reed/answers_json/1353@2/d: I am the candidate who brings the reasonable, tested ideas of sound money, protection, and prosperity. Bryan on the other hand will usher in radicalism and instability.
en.1896_McKinley_Reed/answers_json/1354@3/d: My campaign will reach out to workers across the American spectrum, while Bryan's policies will leave them defenseless against foreign competition and will debase their wages.
en.1896_McKinley_Reed/answers_json/1355@4/d: My administration will bring back the era of the budget surplus, and will work towards the professionalization of the federal government. We will continue to phase out the 'spoils system' in accordance with the Pendleton Act.
en.1896_McKinley_Reed/answers_json/1356@5/d: I appreciate the faith of the American people and consult always with the Lord before I make my decisions. I will run a moderate, sensible agenda that appeals to the broad majority.
en.1896_McKinley_Reed/answers_json/1357@6/d: Labor agitators and agrarian radicals are threatening to overthrow our system of government. They have put forward a preposterous array of Constitutional Amendments and confiscatory welfare programs.
en.1896_McKinley_Reed/answers_json/1358@7/d: Democrats who believe in the gold standard are welcome in our party. We will increase tariffs, to be sure, but in a moderate way that addresses their concerns.
en.1896_McKinley_Reed/answers_json/1359@8/d: William Jennings Bryan makes an eloquent appeal to the heart. It's important for voters to realize that his solutions will not help our country.
en.1896_McKinley_Reed/answers_json/1360@9/d: Bryan's naked ambition knows no bounds. It is unbecoming of a candidate to make campaign appearances on his own behalf.
en.1896_McKinley_Reed/answers_json/1361@10/: There's no way I can compete with Bryan's oratorical talents. Instead, I will receive groups of visitors at my home in Canton, Ohio. We have the financing to pay for these visits, and anyone who shows up will receive a free sandwich while I deliver a speech.
en.1896_McKinley_Reed/answers_json/1365@11/: Bryan combines vague, non-sensical appeals to emotion with a near-blasphemous use of religious symbolism. I'm confident that the voters will reject this demagogue.
en.1896_McKinley_Reed/answers_json/1366@12/: Free coinage of silver will debase our currency and make a mockery of us to the rest of the world.
en.1896_McKinley_Reed/answers_json/1367@13/: William Jennings Bryan is a devout, honest man. It's unfortunate that he proposes such misguided policies.
en.1896_McKinley_Reed/answers_json/1368@14/: Our campaign is much better positioned to address the concerns of ordinary Americans than Bryan's. He is overly focused on the silver issue.
en.1896_McKinley_Reed/answers_json/1369@15/: I can't attack Bryan like the papers can without losing some of my luster. Let them publish the defamatory cartoons and opinion pieces.
en.1896_McKinley_Reed/answers_json/1370@16/: The big newspapers should remind the voters that I represent a return to prosperity after the Democratic disaster of the previous four years. They should be paying as little attention to Bryan as possible.
en.1896_McKinley_Reed/answers_json/1371@17/: I'm not comfortable coordinating my message with the press. I trust that they will find the right way to present a contrast between me and my opponent.
en.1896_McKinley_Reed/answers_json/1372@18/: Absolutely not. Can you imagine how it would look if we removed ourselves from the ticket in any state? And for an old man like Palmer?
en.1896_McKinley_Reed/answers_json/1373@19/: If Palmer will remove himself from the ballot in Kentucky, Indiana, West Virginia, Maryland, and Delaware, then I will give him free reign in the Deep South.
en.1896_McKinley_Reed/answers_json/1374@20/: I hope Palmer will see fit to remove himself unilaterally from the most hotly contested border states. His is purely a protest candidacy however, and I cannot remove myself from a ballot on his behalf without looking like a buffoon.
en.1896_McKinley_Reed/answers_json/1375@21/: I am willing to make an expansive deal with Palmer. He may remain on the ballot in Illinois, but must remove himself completely from the other northern states. In turn I will give him free reign in the entire South.
en.1896_McKinley_Reed/answers_json/1399@22/: Bryan would drive the important railroads of this region, such as Union Pacific, into bankruptcy by reneging on agreed-upon financing arrangements.
en.1896_McKinley_Reed/answers_json/1400@23/: Bryan is the type of do-gooder politician who would attempt to impose his own morality on this independent region.
en.1896_McKinley_Reed/answers_json/1401@24/: One of my highest priorities in office will be a canal through Nicaragua, which will greatly enhance our national trade. Democrats lack the ambition for such far-reaching projects.
en.1896_McKinley_Reed/answers_json/1402@25/: Much of California's livelihood comes from gold mining. I reject any call to undermine gold through the free coinage of silver.
en.1896_McKinley_Reed/answers_json/1408@26/: There is a certain element of conservatism in the southern states. I don't think that their temperament aligns with that of Bryan. I will simply repeat the message that he is a radical.
en.1896_McKinley_Reed/answers_json/1409@27/: As a Civil War veteran, I am uniquely positioned to preach a message of sectional unity and Americanism. These states must know that we have allowed bygones to be bygones.
en.1896_McKinley_Reed/answers_json/1410@28/: There is a burgeoning textile industry in the Upper South. Their success depends on cheap cotton, protection, and an absence of destabilizing labor issues.
en.1896_McKinley_Reed/answers_json/1411@29/: I will remind them that we support Cuban independence.
en.1896_McKinley_Reed/answers_json/1415@30/: We are running a 45-state strategy. I want our victory and repudiation of the silver Democrats to be as large as possible.
en.1896_McKinley_Reed/answers_json/1416@31/: That's not a good idea. Let's be realistic and devote our efforts to the states that matter.
en.1896_McKinley_Reed/answers_json/1455@32/: Our speakers should converge on Illinois from all directions. We need to blanket this state with advertising and with political parades.
en.1896_McKinley_Reed/answers_json/1456@33/: Let's take the fight to Bryan. I want us to be campaigning the hardest in Missouri, Nebraska, Kansas, and Iowa. Our extra cash will ensure a landslide on election night.
en.1896_McKinley_Reed/answers_json/1457@34/: Let's continue to focus on the Midwest. Ohio, Illinois, Indiana, Michigan, etc.
en.1896_McKinley_Reed/answers_json/1458@35/: I want us to put all of our spare resources into Iowa and Minnesota.
en.1896_McKinley_Reed/answers_json/1459@36/: We need to shore up our base. Let's make sure we win in Pennsylvania and New York, where the stakes are highest.
en.1896_McKinley_Reed/answers_json/1460@37/: I support a strict adherence to the gold standard, which is fundamental to American prosperity.
en.1896_McKinley_Reed/answers_json/1461@38/: Limited silver coinage is a good compromise. I support a program like that of Bland-Allison where the government purchases around $2 million of silver each month.
en.1896_McKinley_Reed/answers_json/1462@39/: I support the free, unlimited coinage of silver at the current market price of 30-to-1 against gold. This ratio should be frequently adjusted to match actual prices in order to avoid another run on the Treasury's gold supply.
en.1896_McKinley_Reed/answers_json/1463@40/: I support the free, unlimited coinage of silver at a fixed price ratio of 16-to-1 against gold.
en.1896_McKinley_Reed/answers_json/1464@41/: Tariffs should be limited to the minimum amount necessary to raise sufficient revenue for the federal government.
en.1896_McKinley_Reed/answers_json/1465@42/: In limited areas where we have new industries forming, tariffs can be higher. They should be low on most products.
en.1896_McKinley_Reed/answers_json/1466@43/: Where we have mature, stable industries, tariffs can be lower. They should be high on most products.
en.1896_McKinley_Reed/answers_json/1467@44/: We need high tariffs on a variety of products and commodities to stimulate American manufacturing.
en.1896_McKinley_Reed/answers_json/1468@45/: The Democratic idea has been that if you legislate to make the masses prosperous, their prosperity will find its way up through every class which rests upon them. We need to help our farmers and our workers by allowing the coinage of silver.
en.1896_McKinley_Reed/answers_json/1469@46/: It's time we think about implementing a series of public works projects to occupy our excess labor force. This will improve business by placing more money in the hands of consumers.
en.1896_McKinley_Reed/answers_json/1470@47/: I can't stress this enough. The most important thing we can do right now is increase our tariffs to protect American business.
en.1896_McKinley_Reed/answers_json/1471@48/: We need to reaffirm our commitment to non-intervention in business affairs. Companies need stability before they will have the confidence to expand.
en.1896_McKinley_Reed/answers_json/1472@49/: This was the act of a tyrant. Pullman was engaged in abominable business practices, and in the darkest hour Cleveland cast his lot with the company over the working man.
en.1896_McKinley_Reed/answers_json/1473@50/: Governor Altgeld was working to mediate the dispute between the Pullman Company and the strikers when Cleveland interfered. There should have absolutely been more time given for these sides to reach an accommodation.
en.1896_McKinley_Reed/answers_json/1474@51/: It's not the job of government to regulate labor disputes, but the fact of the matter is that these strikers were allowing no rail traffic to pass through Chicago whatsoever. Something needed to be done.
en.1896_McKinley_Reed/answers_json/1475@52/: Bargaining for wages is the business of a man and his employer. Collective bargaining has no place in American society, and I commend Grover Cleveland for having the courage to act decisively.
en.1896_McKinley_Reed/answers_json/1476@53/: It is my dream to see a Prohibition Amendment passed before I die.
en.1896_McKinley_Reed/answers_json/1477@54/: These measures are a step in the right direction. Nothing destroys so many lives in this country as does the pernicious habit of drinking alcohol.
en.1896_McKinley_Reed/answers_json/1478@55/: Perhaps if our goal is to prevent drinking on Sunday, or public drunkenness, I am all for those measures. But a blanket temperance law is a different story.
en.1896_McKinley_Reed/answers_json/1480@56/: Anyone who knows me should know the answer to this question. I support the free coinage of silver at a price ratio of 16-to-1 versus gold.
en.1896_McKinley_Reed/answers_json/1481@57/: I support the coinage of silver, and this action was a step in the wrong direction. It took money out of the system when we needed it the most, and is partly to blame for the depth of our current downturn.
en.1896_McKinley_Reed/answers_json/1482@58/: Unfortunately the Treasury was bankrupt. I do think that Cleveland approached this in the usual heavy-handed, abrasive manner, but he was absolutely in the right. This whole episode demonstrates the folly of silver coinage.
en.1896_McKinley_Reed/answers_json/1483@59/: We can criticize Cleveland for a lot of things, but his repeal of the Silver Purchase Act is not one of them. I supported Cleveland all the way in the repeal debate.
en.1896_McKinley_Reed/answers_json/1494@60/: We would also like to move a little more in the direction of lower tariffs, but overall this is a good law.
en.1896_McKinley_Reed/answers_json/1495@61/: I am disappointed with the half measures taken in this act. If Senators were directly elected by the people, they would be less beholden to the types of financial interests who wrote their own tariffs into this law.
en.1896_McKinley_Reed/answers_json/1496@62/: This act was the result of countless hours of compromise and negotiations. It's time we closed this issue and stopped changing our entire tariff system every time a new Administration takes over.
en.1896_McKinley_Reed/answers_json/1497@63/: My first action as President will be to reinstate higher tariffs. This is an American policy that supports American factories and American workers.
en.1896_McKinley_Reed/answers_json/1507@64/: When I am President, you will finally have someone who takes our antitrust legislation seriously. I will break up monopolistic banks and railroads in places where they stifle competition.
en.1896_McKinley_Reed/answers_json/1508@65/: I take a very narrow view of the term "monopoly". There is a need for these statutes but they open up a lot of danger for political witch hunts.
en.1896_McKinley_Reed/answers_json/1509@66/: I favor a hands-off approach to the economy. The federal government has no business stepping in and breaking a company into pieces.

en.1896_McKinley_Reed/answers_json/1513@70/: I doubt that it is even Constitutional for the federal government to control railroad rates. This will never happen in my Administration.

en.1896_McKinley_Reed/answers_json/1547@73/: It is the responsibility of the worker to put aside such funds as are necessary to protect them from these events. This is why we have mutual aid societies in place.
en.1896_McKinley_Reed/answers_json/1548@74/: Not only would this greatly improve working conditions for Americans, it would increase employment by spreading our working hours amongst more people.
en.1896_McKinley_Reed/answers_json/1549@75/: I am a strong supporter of labor, but I also think that working hour restrictions are more appropriate for women and children than for grown men.
en.1896_McKinley_Reed/answers_json/1550@76/: I do not see the authority for regulating this under the Commerce Clause of the Constitution. This is something that individual states would need to investigate.

en.1896_McKinley_Reed/answers_json/1586@78/: If we could manage it, I would increase the number of justices on the Court so that we can dissipate the influence of the reactionaries presently in control there.

en.1896_McKinley_Reed/answers_json/1603@82/: It was stock market and railroad company chicanery which caused the Panic of 1893. Sensible regulation of this process could have saved us all a lot of trouble.
en.1896_McKinley_Reed/answers_json/1604@83/: The New York Stock Exchange is a private company providing liquidity to other companies. The last thing our fragile economy needs is some hare-brained intervention in this process.
